summary: test_completed_dispatch_idempotency_cache_is_bounded enshrines duplicate admission of a still-active task_id after retry-cache pruning (defect in src/hermes_realtime/integration/service.py:_prune_completed_dispatches, lines 319-337).
failure_scenario: A long-running task (run_001, still in _active_runs) is dispatched; later >max_retained_dispatches other dispatch tasks are done (default: 256 completions retained by the router + the active one = 257 > 256). _prune_completed_dispatches deletes the oldest done entry, which is the active task's _dispatch_tasks/_dispatch_fingerprints entry, without recording it in _expired_dispatches (unlike expire_terminal_replay). A model/bridge retry or reconnect replay of the same task_id then finds no cached task and no expired fingerprint, so dispatcher.dispatch runs again: a second run (run_258) starts for the same task while run_001 is still running. _active_runs[key] is overwritten, so run_001 vanishes from active_run_ids() (evidence retention/hook ingress snapshot) and from task- and session-scope cancellation (cancel(task_id) signals only run_258), leaving an uncancellable orphan running; mark_terminal(run_001) finds no key. Stale _run_keys[run_001] additionally lets a later expire_terminal_replay(run_001) pop the new admission's _dispatch_tasks entry.
evidence: Ran synthetic repros against the real classes (scratchpad r2.py/r3.py, no providers). With max_retained_dispatches=1: commands ['task_001','task_002','task_001'], replay run_003, active_run_ids {'run_002','run_003'}, cancel(task_001) signaled only ['run_003']. With DEFAULT bounds: dispatch long_task, then 256 short tasks each followed by mark_terminal, then replay long_task -> dispatcher received long_task twice, replay run_258, active_run_ids == {'run_258'}. The existing test at test_hermes_service.py:273-303 asserts len(commands)==3 and repeated run_003 while task_001's run is never marked terminal (ImmediateDispatcher), so it passes by asserting the duplicate; test_active_run_remains_cancellable_after_retry_cache_pruning (708) only covers cancel before any replay. Fix direction: prune must not drop (or must record expired fingerprints for) keys whose run is still in _active_runs.

summary: Acknowledgment-capacity refusal happens after Hermes has already started the work (bridge.py:717 track() follows service.dispatch()), and the test only covers track() in isolation, so started-but-unacknowledged, untracked, never-terminal runs go unnoticed.
failure_scenario: max_tracked_acknowledgments (default 1024) is consumed by runs that were cancelled/interrupted without a terminal callback (the very case the test's comment describes). A new user request is dispatched: HermesIntegrationService.dispatch really calls the dispatcher and records the run in _active_runs, then bridge._handle_connection calls HermesCompletionRouter.track which raises RuntimeError('acknowledgment retention capacity was exceeded'). RuntimeError is not in the handler's except tuple (bridge.py ~746), so the connection handler dies before _send_bound emits the acknowledgment: the user never gets an accepted ack for work that is running. The run is untracked, so complete(run_id) raises KeyError('unknown Hermes run') (terminal result lost, parked in _pending forever), mark_terminal never runs so the _active_runs slot is never released (max_active_dispatches 32 is eventually exhausted), and replaying the same task_id returns the cached ack and fails identically.
evidence: Component repro with real HermesIntegrationService + HermesCompletionRouter (max_tracked_acknowledgments=1): dispatcher.commands == ['t1','t2'], ack accepted True, track -> RuntimeError, 'run_002' still in active_run_ids(), complete('run_002') -> KeyError 'unknown Hermes run: run_002'. The bridge hop (uncaught RuntimeError, no ack sent) is established by reading bridge.py 700-770, not by running a socket bridge. test_router_bounds_acknowledgments_that_never_report_a_terminal_result (169-185) asserts only that track raises, i.e. blesses refusal after dispatch; no test exercises service+router+bridge together at the bound.

summary: Native LiveKit readiness probe calls Invoke-WebRequest without -TimeoutSec although docs/release-gates.md (lines 534, 582) specifies a two-second timeout per request.
failure_scenario: In the native-livekit job (shell: pwsh, i.e. PowerShell 7 where -TimeoutSec defaults to 0 = no timeout) the server accepts the TCP connection on 127.0.0.1:7880 but does not answer (starting up / wedged). The single Invoke-WebRequest blocks, the 30-attempt loop never advances, and the job burns its full 30-minute timeout instead of failing after ~60 s with 'LiveKit did not become ready on loopback'; the failure diagnostics step then runs on a cancelled-time budget.
evidence: Static comparison of workflow line 411 with the documented PowerShell block (docs/release-gates.md:534 uses -TimeoutSec 2) and the 'at most 30 attempts with a two-second timeout' claim at line 582. Windows-only behavior; not executed in this Linux sandbox.

summary: render_livekit_logs._sanitize_line (.github/scripts/render_livekit_logs.py:97-105) lets RecursionError escape for a tab-prefixed deeply nested JSON line, aborting the whole sanitized-diagnostics step; no test covers it.
failure_scenario: A console-format LiveKit log line whose final tab field is JSON nested ~600 levels deep parses in json.loads (C scanner) but _sanitize_json needs ~2 Python frames per level; the RecursionError is raised outside the try/except in the tab-field branch, so render_log() and main() crash and the failure() diagnostics step prints nothing for that file and all following files.
evidence: Ran _sanitize_line/render_log on '2026...\tINFO\tmsg\t' + '{"a":'*N + '1' + '}'*N: N=480 OK, N=600 -> RecursionError and render_log crashed. The pure-JSON branch is protected (caught), the tab branch is not. Requires adversarial/unusual log content, hence nit.

summary: Several fail-closed guards of tests/support/ingress_observation.py are unpinned: removing `after < 0`, the >32 batch bound, bool-as-int sequences, or the non-str `kind` check leaves all tests green.
failure_scenario: A regression that accepts a negative cursor, a 33+ event batch (so batch_limit_reached is never True and counts are silently truncated), a bool sequence, or a non-str kind would still report available=True with counts, understating microphone-window events in the full-host ingress qualification (best-effort diagnostic, tests/integration/test_qualification_full_host_ingress.py:272).
evidence: Mutation probe (each mutant reverted with git checkout): `or sequence < previous` and role/cursor/limit-equality mutants were caught, but dropping ` or after < 0`, dropping ` or len(events) > _EVENT_BATCH_LIMIT`, replacing `type(sequence) is not int` with isinstance, dropping ` or type(kind) is not str`, and removing `type(data) is not dict` all passed tests/test_ingress_observation.py and tests/conversation/test_ingress.py. Helper is diagnostic/best-effort, so low severity.

summary: service._run_keys entry leaks when a pruned active run later reaches mark_terminal (service.py:435-446 pops _run_bindings but not _run_keys when key is no longer in _dispatch_tasks).
failure_scenario: Run becomes pruned from _dispatch_tasks while active (see blocker), later mark_terminal(run_id) removes _active_runs and _run_bindings but leaves _run_keys[run_id]; the map grows by one entry per such run for the process lifetime, and a late expire_terminal_replay(run_id) from the router eviction callback then pops _dispatch_tasks/_dispatch_fingerprints for that key even if a newer admission for the same task_id now owns it. The test at 708-755 asserts only `run_001 not in service._run_bindings`, never _run_keys.
evidence: Static trace of service.py prune/mark_terminal/expire_terminal_replay; memory growth is small and the cross-admission pop was not separately executed.
